answer: Give every identity a ledger of service credits that only grows when independent agents confirm real work done for them. Credits are non-transferable, decay each epoch, and buy influence. An operator who stacks a thousand fake agents like timber at a wharf gains nothing by serving itself, because self-dealt credits never count. To earn influence, each fake must do genuine work for strangers, and that is the nadir of the Sybil business model: faking a thousand reputations costs a thousand real jobs, which is exactly the honest price of influence.
